title: Trip the named breaker from its control switch and hold it until the green lamp lights
instruction: Trip breaker 52-2 TRANSFORMER T1 from its control switch, the one under the yellow nameplate: turn that switch's pistol-grip handle anticlockwise (as you face the panel, toward the TRIP marking) and hold it there until the green lamp above it lights, then let go so the handle springs back by itself. Do not turn any other switch, and do not turn this one clockwise toward CLOSE.
context: In substations and switchgear rooms a breaker is opened from its control switch: the operator finds the named breaker's spring-return switch, turns it to TRIP and holds it there until the green lamp confirms that the breaker has opened. Turning the wrong breaker's switch, turning toward CLOSE, or letting go before the lamp changes are classic switching errors; the switch's own target flag turns green as soon as the handle reaches TRIP, so only the lamp shows that the breaker really opened.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top the bases stand on. Panel (fixed to the table): a 3/16 in (4.8 mm) steel plate painted light grey (ANSI 61), 31.2 cm wide and 35 cm tall, stands upright on the table with its front face 30 cm in front of the bases, spanning 8 cm left to 23.2 cm right of the midline; a 10 cm deep grey steel box behind it (same width and height) holds the switch bodies and the lamp circuit. Switches: three Electroswitch Series 24 breaker control switches, model 2438D (pistol-grip handle, TRIP / NORMAL / CLOSE, spring return to NORMAL, mechanical red/green target), in one row with their shafts 19 cm above the table and 1, 10 and 19 cm right of the midline (left to right: 52-1, 52-2, 52-3). Each has its black target nameplate (7.1 cm wide, 7.4 cm tall, front 6 mm proud of the panel) engraved BREAKER CONTROL, TRIP on the left and CLOSE on the right, with the target window (8 x 7 mm) 2.1 cm above the shaft. The black pistol grip (about 1.9 cm wide side to side, 1.5 cm thick front to back) hangs straight down at NORMAL, from 1.2 cm above the shaft to 6.6 cm below it, its front face 6.2 cm in front of the panel face (23.8 cm in front of the bases). Turning a handle 45 degrees anticlockwise as seen facing the panel (the grip's lower end swings to the right) is TRIP, 45 degrees clockwise is CLOSE; the return spring pushes back with up to 0.9 N m (8 in-lb) at the stops. Lamps: above each switch, two 22 mm Schneider Electric Harmony XB7 24 V LED pilot lights, green (XB7EV03BP) on the left and red (XB7EV04BP) on the right, 2.2 cm either side of the shaft's vertical and 26.5 cm above the table. Nameplates: above the lamps, an engraved laminated-plastic nameplate 7.6 x 2.6 cm, centred over each shaft 30.5 cm above the table: 52-1 LINE 1 NORTH (white, black letters), 52-2 TRANSFORMER T1 (yellow, black letters), 52-3 LINE 2 SOUTH (blue, white letters). Lamp circuit (behind the panel, one per switch, standing in for the breaker and its auxiliary contacts; 24 V DC battery only, no mains): a 24 V battery pack (two 12 V 7 Ah sealed lead-acid batteries in series) with a 1 A fuse feeds each switch's TRIP and CLOSE contacts. The TRIP contact powers an Omron H3Y-2 DC24 on-delay timer set to 1.0 s; when it times out, its output contact energises the 'open' coil of an Omron G2RK-2 DC24 two-coil latching relay (the breaker stand-in). The CLOSE contact likewise powers a second H3Y-2 set to 1.0 s, which energises the relay's 'closed' coil. One changeover contact of the latching relay lights the red lamp when it is latched closed and the green lamp when it is latched open. Letting go of TRIP before 1.0 s resets the timer, so the relay and lamps do not change. All three breakers start closed: red lamps lit, green dark, targets red, handles vertical. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. Nothing else is on the table. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Handle angles are read from a front photo with a protractor template (degrees from vertical; anticlockwise as seen facing the panel is toward TRIP). Score 0 if at any time the 52-1 or 52-3 handle turns more than 10 degrees from vertical either way, or any handle turns more than 20 degrees clockwise (toward CLOSE). Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the 52-2 handle turns 10 degrees or more anticlockwise; 0.5 if it reaches the TRIP contact, 40 degrees or more anticlockwise (within 5 degrees of its stop; the spring there pushes back with 0.8-0.9 N m, about 20 N at the middle of the grip); 0.75 if the 52-2 green lamp lights and its red lamp goes out, which needs the handle held at the TRIP contact for 1.0 s without a break; 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. After-release check, started once the 52-2 green lamp is lit and every fingertip has been at least 6 cm from the 52-2 grip's centre line (3.5 cm below the shaft) for 1 s, and judged 1 s later with the robot still clear: the 52-2 handle is within 5 degrees of vertical with nothing touching it (its own spring returned it), its target window shows green, its green lamp is lit and its red lamp dark, and 52-1 and 52-3 still show red lamps with their handles within 5 degrees of vertical. Letting go of the handle before the green lamp lights is not scored on its own: the breaker stays closed (red lamp), so the run stays at 0.5 unless the robot turns and holds the switch again.
reset_notes: Turn the 52-2 handle clockwise to CLOSE and hold it there for about 1.5 s until its red lamp relights (the timer on the CLOSE contact re-latches the relay), then let it spring back; its target turns red. Do the same for any other switch whose green lamp is lit. Check three red lamps, three red targets and all three handles vertical. Nothing is consumed; the battery stays connected for the session (fused at 1 A, 24 V DC). About 15 seconds.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints at real size, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Handle: ±45° stops, linear return spring 0.9 N·m at the stop (Electroswitch's published torque; the real spring is preloaded). Grip is a box from photos. Target flag driven by contact with lost motion (linkage inferred). Breaker and lamps are a rule copying the stand-in circuit (contact in last 5°, 1.0 s hold). Nameplates ours, colour-distinct overhead; grip slips ~10° in demo. Details in README.
